name: scenario-first
title: Claude Writes the Scenario First
kicker: A hook blocks production code until a feature file changes
html:
Claude Writes the Scenario First

Scenario Outline: A library whose policy file renews <weeks> weeks at a time
                  moves the due date that far
  Given the library's policy file reads "<policy>"
  When Ana renews loan 3311
  Then the answer is 200
  And loan 3311 is due "<due>", renewed 1 time

  Examples:
    | policy           | weeks | due        |
    | renewal.weeks=3  | 3     | 2026-12-03 |
    | renewal.weeks=0  | 0     | 2026-11-12 |
    | renewal.weeks=6  | 6     | 2026-12-24 |
    | # no rules       | 3     | 2026-12-03 |

Four rows anyone can read. Remember the zero-weeks row.

gherkin-first.sh
say: Here's what came back first: not code, a scenario. And it's a table, which is the point. Four rows. A policy of three weeks moves the due date three weeks. Zero weeks doesn't move it at all. Six weeks moves it six. And a policy file with no rule keeps three. Anyone in this room can read that, and so can a librarian. Could Claude have skipped this and gone straight to the code? It could have tried. A hook runs before every edit: if the file is production code and no feature file has changed, the edit is refused, and the model reads why. Remember that zero-weeks row. It comes back at the end.

deck:ref.name: right-behavior
deck:ref.label: RIGHT-BEHAVIOR
deck:ref.title: Right behavior: only what the state allows, and a reason when not
deck:ref.summary: The agent is offered only the acts the current state allows, sends each one with the validator from the state it read, and gets a reason when an act is absent. At the small scale it is a Gherkin scenario that says what right means before any code is written.

deck:fragment.name: gherkin-first
deck:fragment.label: No production write until a feature file changes (core/gherkin-first.sh)
deck:fragment.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PreToolUse (Edit|Write|MultiEdit). Blocks a write to production code unless
# a feature file already has an in-flight change, or the author switched
# refactor mode on (scripts/refactor-mode). Exit 2 blocks the tool call
# and sends stderr back to Claude.
set -o pipefail
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

file_path=$(bdd_hook_file_path)
[ -n "$file_path" ] || exit 0
bdd_has_config || exit 0
bdd_load

rel=$(bdd_rel "$file_path")
bdd_is_prod "$rel" || exit 0
bdd_features_dirty && exit 0
# The author switched refactor mode on: pre-commit checks its own terms.
bdd_refactor_on && exit 0

cat >&2 <<EOF
Blocked: about to modify production code ($rel) with no feature file change in this changeset yet.
Write or update the Gherkin scenario first, run the BDD suite to see it fail, then implement.
Feature patterns: $(bdd_list featurePatterns | tr '\n' ' ')
EOF
exit 2

self.title: No production write until a feature file changes (core/gherkin-first.sh)
